_about: match_rules rule 5 (qualifier_conflict): a word in a requirement's SUBJECT that says WHICH side, part or location of a quantity it is about. When the subject carries one and the datasheet field name does not, the pairing is refused ('the maximum external design pressure' is not the sheet's 'Design pressure'; 'the operating pressure of the jacket' is not its 'Operating pressure'). Found on the real PSV review, 2026-10-10. Generic: no standard, document or equipment named. A refusal leaves the requirement unpaired (an engineer's question), never a verdict, so a word here errs towards caution. Checked only next to the field's own words (before them, or after through 'of (the)'). 'nozzle' is NOT a qualifier: a nozzle is the item a field names (N1 size), not a side of it. derived_after: a word RIGHT AFTER the field's own words that makes it a different quantity ('set pressure TOLERANCE' is not the sheet's 'Set pressure'; 'pressure DROP' is not 'Pressure'). Found when the F-b re-read gave the PSV's set pressures values: two ASME VIII tolerance rules read COMPLIANT against the set pressure itself.
_about_quantity_kind: match_rules rule 6 (same quantity kind, order 139): a requirement pairs only with a datasheet value of the same quantity kind. quantity_nouns: the noun that NAMES a quantity, mapped to the claims.unit_dimension family its units already belong to - a LIST when the quantity is stated in more than one (vibration as a velocity or a displacement, flow as a volume or a mass per time), and a noun never refuses a unit that gives one of its kinds (claims holds the units; this holds only the words) - read only when a side states no unit (a statement, a blank field). Two different kinds refuse the pair; a kind that cannot be told, or a subject or medium word the field does not share ('weld joint' efficiency, 'flushing liquid' temperature), holds the pair for an engineer - never a verdict. subject_nouns: nouns naming ANOTHER THING whose quantity a requirement states - a medium (liquid, oil, steam) or a component with its own quantities (joint, seal, bearing). 'weld' is not one: a weld joint is the joint a datasheet's 'Joint efficiency' already names. One of these before the field's words that the field does not share holds the pair for an engineer; an adjective or state word (rated, normal, design, operating, maximum) or a part of the same equipment (shaft, casing) never does. Generic: no standard, document or equipment named. phrase_end: words that end the noun phrase naming a quantity ('the width OF the bearing surface'); determiners: words that open one and mean nothing of their own; generic_heads: words that end a phrase without naming its quantity. Every word in quantity_nouns (_why_quantity_nouns) and subject_nouns (its value) states why it is true for any document; a word that cannot is not added (order 143(4)).

subject_nouns.ligament: the metal between holes in a plate or shell; its efficiency is not the equipment's

subject_nouns.fluid: a medium: its temperature or pressure is that fluid's, not the equipment's process value

subject_nouns.lubricant: a medium: its temperature or pressure is that fluid's, not the equipment's process value
subject_nouns.lube: the common short spelling of lubricant
subject_nouns.barrier: a seal system's barrier fluid, separate from the pumped or process fluid
subject_nouns.buffer: a seal system's buffer fluid, separate from the pumped or process fluid
subject_nouns.flush: a seal flush stream, separate from the pumped or process fluid
subject_nouns.seal: a seal has its own pressures, temperatures and leakage, not the equipment's
subject_nouns.bearing: a bearing has its own temperature, vibration and life, not the process's
subject_nouns.gland: a gland or packing has its own pressure and leakage
subject_nouns.coupling: a coupling has its own rating, torque and service factor
subject_nouns.gasket: a gasket has its own stress, width and rating
subject_nouns.bolt: a bolt has its own stress, load and size
subject_nouns.bolting: the bolting of a joint: its stress and load, not the equipment's
subject_nouns.flange: a flange has its own rating, stress and thickness
subject_nouns.driver: the driver (motor or turbine) has its own power, speed and efficiency
subject_nouns.gearbox: a gearbox has its own power, speed and efficiency
